title: Numeric conversions
recap: Numeric conversions may change range or precision. Converting a finite floating value to an integer discards its fractional part toward zero rather than rounding to the nearest integer.
The source value must fit the destination range. Checking or clamping the source before conversion avoids an out-of-range floating-to-integer conversion.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement wholeDegrees(temperature). Clamp a finite double to [-100,100], then return its integer part truncated toward zero. Tested values are finite and between -10000 and 10000. Clamp before converting so the target integer conversion is always in range.
hints: Handle values outside the allowed range first.
Use an explicit conversion only after the range is safe.
Negative fractions truncate toward zero too.
